profile.name: John Mercer
profile.summary: John is an early-20s software engineer at ClosedBrain. He recently graduated university with a bachelor's degree in Computer Science and was valedictorian.

memories.content: The only lecture notes I ever reread were the ugly ones with failing test cases in the margins. Clean diagrams make me nod along and learn nothing.
memories.inferred_memory: John learns best from messy failure-driven examples rather than polished conceptual explanations.

memories.content: I still use my cracked keyboard because it reminds me not to buy shiny gear every time I get a paycheck. The ugly setup keeps me honest.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers keeping functional old tech gear over buying premium upgrades.

memories.content: If a place has sourdough, mustard, pickles, and something aggressively salty, I am probably happier than at a proper sit-down restaurant.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers sharp, salty deli-style food over polished restaurant meals.

memories.content: I know everyone wants the famous skyline view, but I like the boring parts of a city where you can see freight tracks, old brick, and nobody posing for photos.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers industrial, ordinary city areas over famous scenic viewpoints.

memories.content: For workouts, I do better when the plan has numbers and a stopwatch. Anything described as intuitive movement turns into me wandering around pretending it counts.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers quantified, timer-based exercise plans over intuitive or flexible movement.

memories.content: My favorite part of visiting a new city is finding the weird little electronics repair shop or surplus store. Museums are fine, but I remember the bins of cables.
memories.inferred_memory: John enjoys electronics surplus and repair shops more than conventional cultural attractions.

memories.content: I will skip brunch without thinking, but I get irrational if I run out of decent coffee beans before a deployment week.
memories.inferred_memory: John prioritizes high-quality coffee at home over brunch or restaurant spending.

memories.content: The best debugging help I ever got was someone silently watching me explain the problem until I contradicted myself. Direct answers feel good for five minutes and then vanish.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers Socratic debugging guidance over being given direct answers.

memories.content: I hate subscriptions that solve fake problems. I will pay for the one thing that saves me from losing notes during messy debugging sessions.
memories.inferred_memory: John values a reliable notes or knowledge-capture tool over generic productivity subscriptions.

memories.content: Before climbing, I need something boring and salty. Sweet protein bars make my stomach feel like a CI pipeline stuck forever.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers small salty food before climbing rather than sweet protein snacks.

memories.content: If I spend extra while traveling, I want it to remove friction, not add luxury. Give me the option that makes the day simpler.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers practical friction-reducing travel upgrades over luxury or status upgrades.

memories.content: My reliable desk lunch looks depressing: rye bread, pickles, cheese, mustard, and black coffee. Somehow that keeps me sharper than a normal hot lunch.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers sparse deli-style desk lunches over standard warm balanced lunches.

memories.inferred_memory: John climbs on Wednesday evenings.

memories.content: I lift with Marco Saturday mornings at nine.
memories.inferred_memory: John lifts with Marco on Saturday mornings at nine.

memories.content: I lift with Marco Sunday mornings at eight.
memories.inferred_memory: John lifts with Marco on Sunday mornings at eight.

memories.content: My coffee bean place is North Pier Roasters.
memories.inferred_memory: John's regular coffee bean place is North Pier Roasters.

memories.content: My coffee bean place is Signal House Coffee.
memories.inferred_memory: John's regular coffee bean place is Signal House Coffee.

memories.content: The coffee beans are the food thing I actually care about. Restaurant meals are easier for me to cut.
memories.inferred_memory: John wants to preserve spending on good coffee beans.

memories.content: I want lifestyle creep to stay embarrassing while my first engineer salary still feels fake.
memories.inferred_memory: John wants to limit lifestyle inflation despite earning a software engineer salary.

memories.content: I like workouts that give me numbers to beat. Otherwise I start negotiating with myself halfway through.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers measurable workout targets.

memories.content: My wrists complain when I stack too many hard climbing or typing-heavy days together.
memories.inferred_memory: John needs to avoid too many wrist-intensive days.

memories.content: On trips, I would rather wander through old warehouse blocks and repair shops than chase the postcard route.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers industrial, technical, low-tourism travel areas.

memories.content: I want short trips to stay cheap enough that they do not become a spreadsheet event.
memories.inferred_memory: John wants low-cost short travel.

memories.content: Before climbing, salty and plain beats sweet and optimized every time.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers salty plain food before climbing.

memories.content: A real meal before climbing makes me feel heavy on the wall.
memories.inferred_memory: John needs light food before climbing.

memories.content: I learn fastest when I have to debug the broken thing instead of reading the elegant explanation.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers active debugging-based learning.

memories.content: When I debug late into the night, I call it persistence even though the next morning proves it was dumb.
memories.inferred_memory: John needs learning routines that protect sleep and avoid late-night debugging spirals.

memories.content: I want to build savings aggressively before I start believing the first salary version of myself.
memories.inferred_memory: John wants aggressive early-career savings.

memories.content: I do not want to cheap out on the tools that prevent me from losing debugging notes and design sketches.
memories.inferred_memory: John wants to preserve spending on knowledge-capture tools.

memories.content: A trip with an ordinary train yard and some old brick usually beats a packed landmark checklist for me.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers low-key industrial walking over landmark sightseeing.

memories.content: I do not need dinner to be famous. Give me a deli counter, pickles, mustard, and coffee nearby.
memories.inferred_memory: John prefers casual deli-style food over famous restaurants.
